title: The boy who kept one name
hookLine: a boy won't stop saying one name, and his father wants him to
carry: the Lord lives in every being
tomorrow: is Vishnu in the pillar? the king is about to find out.

lines: TELL ME THE BEST THING YOU LEARNED.
cards: Some kids come home and announce what they learned at school whether anyone asked or not. This one gets asked. A king lifts his small son onto his lap and says: tell me the best thing your teachers have taught you.
And the boy, Prahlada, answers without blinking. The best thing is to remember Vishnu. The king goes cold.
Vishnu is the god who killed his brother. The teachers swear they never taught the boy that. Prahlada says nobody had to.

teach.b: The king is Hiranyakashipu, and in the Bhagavata Purana he has made himself nearly impossible to kill. His kingdom has one rule: no one worships Vishnu. His own son breaks it, cheerfully, out loud.
So the king tries to get rid of the problem.
In the telling, Prahlada is thrown before elephants, given to snakes, fed poison, dropped from a height, and each time he comes through. But here's the part worth telling a friend tonight.
In between all that, the boy goes back to school, and when the teachers step out, he teaches the other children. They're the sons of demons, raised to fight the gods.

teach.h: RECESS: THE LORD IS IN EVERYONE.
teach.b: And Prahlada tells them: the Lord lives in every being, in you, in me, in anyone you'd call an enemy. Dividing the world into mine and not mine, friend and enemy, comes from a confused mind.
So be a friend to every creature.
Then he goes further: being born a god, a sage or into a fine family isn't what counts. Anyone at all can turn toward the Lord. A child in a demon's palace, saying the circle has no outside.
Then the king calls him in one more time and points at a stone pillar in the hall. If your Vishnu is everywhere, he says, is he in this?

how: In some Hindu families Prahlada's story is retold around Holi, and Narasimha Jayanti marks the evening the man-lion appeared; children often meet Prahlada as the boy who would not stop remembering Vishnu.

o: the stone pillar in the demon king's hall
Vishnu as the man-lion, half man and half lion
a lion-shaped demon king who fought Vishnu

games.q: who's who in the palace — tap the pairs.
p: the king: no one worships Vishnu
the son who keeps remembering Vishnu
swear they never taught him that
hear the Lord lives in everyone

s: Prahlada's story is about a boy who fought his father
he never fights back. he keeps one name, and teaches the other children that the Lord lives in everyone.
Prahlada tells the demon boys that friend and enemy is a confused way to see
the Lord lives in every being, he says, so be a friend to every creature.
Prahlada learned his devotion from his teachers
the teachers swear they never taught it; he says nobody had to.

games.q: your friends tease you for a small habit you keep: a thank-you before meals, a page you read each night. by Prahlada's story, what fits?
o: keep it, openly, without turning it into a fight.
keep it only at home, where nobody can make fun of it.
argue back until they respect it; that's what he did.
games.why: Prahlada never hides his devotion and never turns on his father. steady and out loud, and gentle with everyone, even the demon boys.

practice: Pick one sound around you, a fridge humming, traffic, a bird, your own breath, and stay with just that sound for the sit. When your mind wanders off to judge it, nice or annoying, come back to simply hearing it.
One steady thing to listen for, the way Prahlada kept one name.

wordCard.voice: Narasimha: Vishnu as the man-lion, from nara, man, and simha, lion. He hasn't arrived yet. Prahlada is still standing by the pillar.

orig.note: Sanskrit: nara, man, plus simha, lion. The man-lion form of Vishnu.

carryVoice: Hold on to it: the Lord lives in every being. A child in a demon's palace said so. Back tomorrow.

sources.ref: Bhagavata Purana 7.2 (Hiranyakashipu's grief and anger over his brother Hiranyaksha, killed by Vishnu as the boar)
Bhagavata Purana 7.4–7.5 (Hiranyakashipu's rule; Prahlada's answer on his father's lap; the teachers; the attempts on his life)
Bhagavata Purana 7.6–7.7 (Prahlada teaches his classmates: the Lord in every being, friendship to every creature, birth is not what counts)
